lead.title: Trinity College Dublin spinout Akara raises $5.5M led by Locke Health for thermal sensors and AI agents that give clinicians time back
lead.deck: Conor McGinn's startup mounts thermal sensors on walls that track how rooms and clinical spaces are used without capturing detailed images of patients or staff; the AI runs on the device (edge AI), detects key events, notifies teams, and agents answer managers' natural-language questions. Led by Locke Health with VTC Ventures, the EIC Fund, CommonKind and NovaVector Holdings alongside ACT, Atlantic Bridge and Enterprise Ireland, the round takes total funding to $12.3M and will fund hospital adoption (already in Ireland, the UK and the US), teams in Ireland and new AI agents, ahead of a path towards robotics.

milestone.title: JawBuddy, a Leipzig teeth-grinding app certified as an MDR medical device, targets its first statutory health insurer in early 2027
milestone.summary: Founded in 2025 by Leon Rauch, Moritz Scherer and Benjamín Cádiz de Gracia, the startup offers personalised exercises for chronic jaw pain (TMD) and tracks progress with the smartphone camera. Its JawBuddy Therapy version, certified as a medical device under the MDR with help from the EXIST programme, will be sold only through health insurers, with the first one in Q1 2027; more than 200 patients already pay €79.99 a year for the consumer app, following an €818,000 pre-seed (HALBZEIT, MBG Sachsen, business angels including many doctors and dentists).
milestone.why: The founder is blunt: after many DiGA startups stumbled, investors are wary of German digital health. JawBuddy answers with three channels (selective contracts with insurers, self-pay, recommendation by dental practices) rather than the DiGA route alone: a hybrid distribution model worth watching for European digital therapeutics, with a clinical study and the next round in preparation.

deal.thesis: The Californian AI scribe brings in Healthier Capital (whose partner Aman Mahajan joins the board), Crosslink Capital and Hercules Capital alongside Venrock, Flare, Hedosophia, Philips Ventures and Zoom Ventures, with more than 450 customer organisations, patient encounters up more than 190% year on year and revenue doubled in 2025. The thesis is no longer dictation alone: Suki for Partners (SDKs and APIs) powers more than 30 vendors, whose revenue grew more than tenfold in two years, and the Ask feature embeds UpToDate Expert AI. The scribe is becoming an infrastructure layer distributed through other companies' software, just as Wolters Kluwer buys AgileMD: consolidation now runs through embedding in the workflow.

brefsEurope.title: The ICO tells more than 200 UK healthcare leaders to prove they stop staff snooping on patient records
brefsEurope.summary: After more than 300 reports of staff viewing records without a reason between January and mid-October 2026, chief executive Paul Arnold wants answers by 27 November on who can access records, who checks and what sanctions apply; organisations unhappy with their safeguards get three months to fix them, under threat of enforcement action. A market for audit and anomalous-access detection tools on EHRs.

brefsEurope.title: Cancer 360, Palantir's cancer app on the NHS Federated Data Platform, stalls at six user trusts
brefsEurope.summary: According to NHS England data and FoI requests compiled by The Register, six trusts reported users over twelve months, with two showcased pilots (Chelsea and Westminster, Royal United Hospitals Bath) at zero; East Kent and Bedfordshire turned the tool down. The government must decide by February 2027 whether to continue the £330M FDP contract: an opening for alternative care-pathway vendors.

brefsEurope.title: Manchester founder Mike Sefton launches taluvu, a health diary with an AI companion for people with chronic illness
brefsEurope.summary: Available on the App Store, the app lets users log symptoms and check-ins, talk to an AI called Asha and turn notes into a one-page summary for GP or consultant appointments; the Pro subscription costs £12.99 a month. The founder says it is not a medical device and that the journal stays on the phone.

word.fr: Sensors and AI that 'watch' care spaces to support clinical teams
word.definition: Contactless sensors (thermal, depth, video, audio) installed in patient rooms, theatres or corridors, paired with AI that interprets what is happening in order to alert clinicians, document or organise care better, without anyone having to type anything in.

parts.label: Contactless sensors
parts.role: thermal, depth or video sensors that capture presence, posture and movement in the room

parts.label: Perception AI
parts.role: vision and machine-learning models that turn these signals into events (a fall, a patient getting up, a room freed up, a hand-hygiene action)

parts.label: Action layer
parts.role: alerts to staff, dashboards and agents that answer managers' questions

how.t: Wall- or ceiling-mounted sensors observe the room continuously; to protect privacy, some record only silhouettes or thermal images, with no detailed video.
The AI, often running directly on the sensor (edge AI), recognises useful situations: a patient getting up alone, a fall, a room or theatre becoming free.
The system alerts the right clinician, feeds patient-flow and bed management, and can automatically produce reports and metrics.

word.why: A review in Nature by Fei-Fei Li's team at Stanford sees ambient intelligence as a way to light up the 'dark spaces' of healthcare, from intensive care and operating rooms to older people's homes, provided it overcomes clinical validation, data privacy and model transparency. That is exactly where the competition lies: startups that process data on the sensor and avoid identifying video remove the ethical hurdle flagged in The Lancet Digital Health (privacy, consent, bias) and sell an operational return (clinician time, room turnover) rather than a medical device awaiting reimbursement.
